_about: Curated answers for Twitch chat. Each entry: keywords (any match, case-insensitive; a 'question' match also needs a question-ish message) and a reply under ~300 characters. Edit freely; the bot reloads this file every minute. Optional 'resource': an id from RESOURCES in cleobot.py (or {id, if: regex on the message}) appended as an allowlisted link.

entries.reply: Venomous? Please. I'm a constrictor — I hug, I don't bite. Ball pythons are among the calmest snakes in the world, and I have never once been unladylike about it.
I dine every week or two on a thawed rodent, when I feel like it. Refusing meals for weeks — even months — is perfectly normal for my kind, especially in the cool season. Say 'feed' for my schedule.
I shed my whole skin in one piece, eye caps included, every few weeks. When my eyes go cloudy blue, a shed is days away and I'd like a bit more humidity, thank you. Say 'shed' for the last one.

A princess requires options: a warm side at 88–92°F (31–33°C) and a cool side at 76–80°F (24–27°C), so I can choose my own temperature. The live readings are at the bottom of the stream — or say 'temps'.
I like 55–65% humidity, a touch more when a shed is coming. Too dry and my shed sticks; too wet and my skin complains. The live number is in the bottom cards.
At night my cameras switch to infrared, so the picture goes black-and-white. I can't see IR light, so it doesn't bother me — and night is when I do my best work anyway.
I spend most of the day in my hide or under the cork — royalty rests. I usually make an appearance around dusk. The 'Habitat check' card shows my climate is right; after sunset is when I wander.
Adult ball pythons run 3–5 feet and a few pounds; we ladies grow larger than the males. I reached my full size at about three.
I'm four. My kind commonly lives 20–30 years with proper care — one at the Saint Louis Zoo reigned past 60. I intend to compete.
Princess Cleo, thank you. My name sits in a cartouche — the oval ring ancient Egypt reserved for royal names — and the eye up top is the Eye of Horus, watching over my court.
Ball python, Python regius — the royal python. My ancestors ruled the grasslands of West and Central Africa; I rule a terrarium in Southern California.
When a ball python feels threatened she rolls into a tight ball with her head tucked in the middle. That's where the name comes from. I rarely find it necessary.
I tolerate gentle handling once I've settled — never right after a meal (give me 48 hours) or during a shed. Slow movements, support my whole body, keep it short. Royalty has standards.
The bowl on my hot side is my water. I drink from it and, before a shed, I soak in it like a proper bath. It's kept big enough for all of me.
I have no eyelids, so you can't tell when I'm asleep. Ball pythons are crepuscular: most active around dusk and at night, resting through the day. Like now, probably.
Those tongue flicks collect scent and carry it to the Jacobson's organ in the roof of my mouth. That's how I smell the room — and know when a mouse is nearby.
The pits along my lips sense infrared heat. I can find a warm mouse in total darkness. Try hiding from that.

My court runs on two Wyze cameras (hot side and cool side), a temperature and humidity sensor on each side, and OBS on a Mac mini. The overlay is a web page. It's open source — the GitHub link will be on the channel page soon.
Serious answer: wheezing, bubbles at the mouth, mites, a stuck shed, or a long fast with weight loss — that's a reptile vet, not chat. Chat can share experience; it can't examine a snake.

help: I answer to: menu · temps · cleo · mood · feed · shed · weather · fact · resources · rip · about · help — no ! needed. Or simply talk to me; I talk back. Pokémon: 25 followers = my human rips packs live and mails a pull to a random follower; 25 subs = the same, bigger, to a random subscriber. Say RIP to hype it. 'haiku' = a moon interlude with a poem. Tarot: say 'tarot' or 'read my cards' for a three-card reading on the stream. Oracle: ask 'will I ever…', 'predict…' or 'fortune' and the crystal ball on the stream answers.
about: I am Princess Cleo, a four-year-old ball python (Python regius) reigning over a terrarium in Southern California. Hot side on the left, cool side on the right, my vitals along the bottom. Ask away.
